name: python_concat_quoted_variable
input: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
reason: String concatenation (+) splices `name` directly into a SELECT statement passed to cursor.execute().

name: python_concat_delete_session
input: cursor.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = " + session_id)
reason: String concatenation splices session_id into a DELETE statement.

name: python_concat_multiple_variables
input: db.execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = '" + status + "' AND id = " + order_id)
reason: Two variables (status, order_id) are concatenated into a SELECT statement reaching db.execute().

name: python_percent_quoted_placeholder
input: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE email = '%s'" % email)
reason: The `%` operator interpolates email directly into the SQL text, unlike the two-argument execute(sql, params) form.

name: python_percent_tuple_operand
reason: The `%` operator is applied to the SQL string with a tuple operand, formatting user_id into the text before it reaches execute().

name: python_percent_multiple_specifiers
input: cursor.execute("UPDATE t SET name = '%s' WHERE id = %d" % (name, id))
reason: Two `%` conversion specifiers are filled in via the % operator before the string reaches execute().

name: python_dot_format_single_placeholder
reason: .format() is chained directly onto the SQL string literal, splicing user_id into the query text.

name: python_dot_format_two_placeholders
input: cursor.execute("UPDATE orders SET status = '{}' WHERE id = {}".format(status, order_id))
reason: .format() fills two placeholders in an UPDATE statement before it reaches execute().

name: python_dot_format_executemany
reason: .format() splices log_id into a DELETE statement passed to executemany().

name: python_fstring_select
reason: The f-string interpolates user_id directly into a SELECT statement passed to execute().

name: python_fstring_delete_quoted
reason: The f-string interpolates token directly into a DELETE statement.

name: python_fstring_django_raw
reason: Django's .raw() executes an f-string-built SELECT statement with an interpolated id.

name: js_template_literal_select
reason: The template literal interpolates userId directly into a SELECT statement passed to db.query().

name: js_template_literal_sequelize
reason: sequelize.query() executes a template literal with status interpolated directly into the SQL text.

name: js_template_literal_knex_raw
reason: knex.raw() executes a template literal with token interpolated directly into a DELETE statement.

name: js_concat_select
input: db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + userId)
reason: String concatenation (+) splices userId directly into a SELECT statement passed to db.query().

name: js_concat_delete
input: connection.query("DELETE FROM logs WHERE id = " + logId)
reason: String concatenation splices logId into a DELETE statement.

name: js_concat_knex_raw
input: db.raw("UPDATE users SET name = '" + name + "' WHERE id = " + userId)
reason: Two variables are concatenated into an UPDATE statement passed to db.raw().

name: clean_qmark_placeholder
reason: The `?` placeholder plus a separate params list is the safe, parameterized form — no interpolation into the SQL text.

name: clean_percent_s_with_params_tuple
reason: `%s` here is the DB driver's own placeholder syntax bound via a separate params tuple (comma, not a `%` operator, follows the SQL string), not string formatting.

name: clean_dollar_positional_param
reason: node-postgres's $1 positional placeholder plus a separate params array binds id safely; nothing is spliced into the string.

name: clean_named_colon_param
input: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = :id", {"id": id})
reason: The :id named placeholder is bound from a separate params dict, not interpolated into the string.

name: clean_named_at_param
input: db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = @id", { id: userId })
reason: The @id named placeholder is bound from a separate params object, not interpolated into the string.

name: clean_orm_filter_django
reason: Django's ORM query builder never assembles a raw SQL string and does not call execute/query/raw.

name: clean_orm_query_builder
reason: A fluent query-builder call chain (.select()/.where()) never constructs or executes a raw SQL string.

name: clean_static_sql_no_variable
input: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true")
reason: A fully static SQL string literal with no variable, concatenation, or interpolation is not injectable.

name: clean_fstring_no_sql_keyword
reason: An f-string with no DB sink call and no SQL keyword is building a file path, not a SQL statement.

name: clean_log_fstring
reason: logger.info() is not a DB sink; the f-string here builds a log message, not SQL.

name: clean_prose_comment_mentions_select
input: # Historical note: this used to run SELECT * FROM users directly via string concat
reason: Bare prose mentioning SELECT and concatenation is not a call-site pattern and must not be flagged.

name: clean_query_selector_false_positive_guard
reason: querySelector() is a DOM API whose name merely starts with "query"; the sink pattern requires "query" immediately followed by `(`, which querySelector( does not satisfy.

name: clean_identifier_containing_query_substring
reason: An identifier merely containing the substring "query" (get_query_count) must not match the .query( sink pattern, which requires a literal `.` immediately before "query".
